method: Tier-0 primary source (allenai.org/blog) fetched directly at publication time per the live-fetch rule for third-party numeric/benchmark citations (policy/verification.md §5). The publication fact is Tier-0-sufficient (confirmed); the cross-model benchmark scores are Ai2's own unreplicated study comparing competitor models (Gemini, Claude, GPT, DeepSeek), so labeled vendor-claim per the independence rule rather than confirmed -- no independent outlet has reproduced or reported the figures.
origin_items: Surfaced during cycle 1's Tier-0 sweep of allenai.org/blog; carried untriaged into cycle 2, opened for verification this cycle.

claims.text: Ai2 published TutorMoments on 7 August 2026, an evaluation framework built from 1,500+ teacher-identified key learning moments across 462 de-identified transcripts of real US math-tutoring sessions covering grades 2-7
claims.reasoning: The fact of publication and the framework's construction are stated directly on Ai2's own blog, Tier 0 and sufficient alone for this announcement/methodology fact.

claims.text: Ai2 tested seven models (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT 5.5, GPT 5.4 mini, and DeepSeek V4 Pro) as tutors on 520 of these moments, split evenly between moments calling for scaffolding and moments calling for pushing rigor
claims.reasoning: Methodology detail from Ai2's own post; not independently reproduced, but presented as the study's own design, not a competitive superiority claim in itself.

claims.text: On appropriate scaffolding, Gemini 2.5 Pro scored highest at 0.896 and GPT 5.4 mini scored lowest at 0.181, against a human-tutor baseline of 0.458; on appropriate rigor, Claude Opus 4.8 scored highest at 0.831 and GPT 5.4 mini lowest at 0.023, against a human baseline of 0.182
claims.reasoning: Cross-lab benchmark scores reported only by Ai2 itself; no independent outlet or third party has reproduced or reported these figures, so labeled vendor-claim per the independence rule despite being fetched live at publication time (satisfying the live-fetch rule for the numbers themselves).

claims.text: Ai2's overall finding is that models tend to over-help and rarely push students toward deeper thinking, though explicit prompting about the trade-off improved every model's scores while still leaving a gap versus human tutoring
claims.reasoning: Ai2's own interpretation of its own results; not independently corroborated.

falsifier_notes: Overall verdict: CLEAR TO PUBLISH with vendor-claim labeling on the benchmark scores/findings (not confirmed) -- headline and TL;DR restricted to the confirmed publication fact only, per style.md Gate 1 (headline must be supported by confirmed claims only). dedup-check returned zero matches (standalone). Search for independent coverage or replication of TutorMoments found none yet (only Ai2's own blog and its self-mirrored Hugging Face post, not an independent source). No dispute or correction found.
